newsitem.title: USA: Rhone-Poulenc Rorer files NDA for Nasacort.
newsitem.headline: Rhone-Poulenc Rorer files NDA for Nasacort.

text.p: Rhone-Poulenc Rorer Inc said Thursday it submitted a New Drug Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for Nasacort HFA (triamcinolone acetonide) Nasal Inhaler, a non-chlorofluorocarbon (CFC) nasal spray to treat seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis symptoms in adults and children six years of age and older.

RPR developed Nasacort HFA -- a reformulation of the currently marketed Nasacort (triamcinolone acetonide) Nasal Inhaler -- in response to an international agreement known as the Montreal Protocol, which calls for the phase-out of products containing ozone-damaging CFC propellants. The new formulation contains tetrafluoroethane (HFA-134a), a safe alternative propellant that has been approved by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) as a replacement for CFCs.

An estimated 26 million Americans, including more than 4 million children, suffer from allergic rhinitis, which produces symptoms including nasal itch, congestion, runny nose, sneezing and watery eyes.
